title: Pan Grilled Rack Of Lamb
description:
It seems like it has just been the last decade or so that you could get these “French-trimmed” lamb racks in the store. They make a wonderful and easy treat as both an elegant meal or something quick and informal (eating these almost like lollipops with you hands!).
After a thorough trimming, there is hardly any fat on these. They’re good with just the most basic spicing of salt and pepper or something a little more elaborate, such as the red wine and rosemary combination suggested here. In the old days, people always had lamb with a mint jelly, and this can be okay in small amounts, but too much mint can overwhelm the delicate lamb flavor.
We have two racks for four people here, but you could very easily have one rack per person.
ingredients: 2 racks of lamb, each 8-9 ribs, about 1 ¼-1 ½ pounds
directions: Put a shallow roasting or jelly roll pan in the oven. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees.
Trim all the fat and silver skin from the racks of lamb.
Season lamb with salt and pepper. Heat a couple of tablespoons of oil in a heavy-bottomed 12-inch skillet over high heat until shimmering.

Place racks of lamb in skillet, meat-side up, with the ribs angled up (over the sides of the pan or balanced against another rack) so that you have good contact between the meat and pan). Cook until well-browned and a nice crust has formed on the surface, about 3 minutes.
Using tongs, flip the racks to meat side down and cooks another 3 minutes.
Transfer lamb to the preheated pan in the oven and roast another 6 minutes (125-130 degrees in the center for medium rare).
When done, take the meat out and put on a serving dish. Cover loosely with foil and let rest 5-10 minutes.
To make the sauce while the lamb is roasting and resting, pour off all but 1 ½ tablespoons fat from skillet used to brown lamb; place skillet over medium heat.
Sauté shallots until softened, about 1 minute. Add red wine and rosemary; increase heat to medium-high and simmer until dark and syrupy, about 7 minutes.
Add chicken broth; simmer until reduced to about ¾ cup, about 5 minutes longer. Remove from heat, swirl in butter; season to taste with salt and pepper.
Carve the lamb, slicing between each rib into individual chops, and serve immediately with the sauce.
